messages:
claire: Hi team - for our POC we need Private deploy with on-prem egress. Netops asks: can you preserve client src IPs? They will also perform TLS inspection.

leo: Short answer: PrivateLink -> we terminate at ENI, so you will see our connector egress IPs. Preserving original TCP src IP end-to-end isn't standard. Options: app proxy that forwards X-Forwarded-For, or a customer-hosted proxy that terminates TLS inside your network.

anya: If they're doing TLS inspection, call out breakage risks (cert pinning, SSO/webhook verification). Recommend advising them not to MITM traffic to Redwood endpoints.

claire: They insist on inspection. Any sample firewall rules we can give them to limit blast radius?

leo: Sample snippet (replace <EGRESS_IPS> / <ENI_CIDR>):
allow tcp from 10.10.0.0/16 to <EGRESS_IPS> 443 comment 'Redwood egress'
allow tcp from 10.10.0.0/16 to <ENI_CIDR> 443 comment 'PrivateLink ENI health'
allow udp from 10.10.0.0/16 to 169.254.169.253 53 comment 'VPC DNS (if required)'

anya: Pricing note: PrivateLink + Private deploy = AWS endpoint hourly + data processing + our egress data charges. If they need static BYOIP egress we can NAT but that adds complexity and likely extra fees.

ops-bot: Docs: https://docs.redwood.inference/private/connectivity (internal) - includes ENI behavior and BYOIP runbook.

claire: Thanks - can we do a 30m sync Wed 11am PT to walk netops through risks and the firewall snippet?

leo: I'll join. Anya?

anya: Yep. I'll bring the security questionnaire items.

claire: Great, see you then :thumbsup:

(End thread)
